headline: Fee growth is swamped by a widening reimbursable-cost gap
summary_short: Choice Hotels' Q1 2026 revenue rose 2.3% y/y to $340.6M, but operating income fell 24.7% to $60.3M and net income dropped 54.4% to $20.3M as a wider reimbursable-expense deficit, higher SG&A, and a $6.2M swing in equity-affiliate losses outweighed fee growth.
summary_long: Revenue rose 2.3% y/y to $340.6M, but operating income fell 24.7% to $60.3M as a larger reimbursable-expense deficit, higher SG&A, and D&A outweighed a $4.6M fee-revenue gain. International royalty fees grew on system expansion and the Choice Hotels Canada acquisition; U.S. royalty fees fell as system-wide RevPAR declined 2.3%. Equity-affiliate losses widened $6.2M and interest expense rose $2.7M, pushing pretax income down $29.5M and net income down 54.4% to $20.3M; diluted EPS fell to $0.44. Operating cash flow swung to -$23.2M from +$20.5M on working-capital timing and higher franchise incentive payments. No FY2026 revenue or EPS guidance was given; the company disclosed a $1.15/share projected 2026 dividend rate and $47.8M of buybacks plus $13.1M of dividends this quarter.

drivers.explanation: Franchise and management fees rose $4.6M, led by a $5.2M increase in international royalty fees and $4.5M more from franchise programs/platforms, partly offset by a $4.0M U.S. royalty-fee decline and $1.5M lower initial fees.
Gross margin fell to 45.6% from 50.5% as cost growth embedded in the wider reimbursable-expense deficit and higher SG&A/D&A outpaced the 2.3% revenue gain.
Operating income fell $19.9M primarily on a $17.5M larger net reimbursable deficit, $3.8M higher SG&A, and $3.1M more depreciation and amortization, partly offset by the $4.6M fee-revenue gain.
Operating margin compressed to 17.7% from 24.0% as the same reimbursable-deficit, SG&A, and D&A increases behind the operating-income decline outpaced revenue growth.

Pretax income fell $29.5M on the operating-income decline plus a $6.2M increase in equity-in-net-loss of affiliates and a $2.7M rise in interest expense; the effective tax rate also rose to 33.0% from 25.5%.
Net margin fell to 6.0% from 13.4% as net income dropped 54% while revenue grew 2.3%, a mechanical effect of shrinking profit against a larger revenue base.
Basic EPS fell to $0.44 from $0.95 as the 54% net-income decline outweighed roughly a 2.3% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares (47.1M to 46.0M) from continued buybacks.
Diluted EPS fell to $0.44 from $0.94 as the net-income decline outweighed the roughly 2.3% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from continued buybacks.

Operating cash flow swung to -$23.2M from +$20.5M on working-capital timing, a $16.5M increase in franchise agreement acquisition cost payments (to $42.8M), and a larger reimbursable deficit, partly offset by lower deferred income taxes.

MD&A attributes the swing chiefly to a $17.5M larger reimbursable-cost deficit and costs tied to the July 2025 Choice Hotels Canada consolidation (added D&A, SG&A, and equity-affiliate losses), against modest underlying fee growth.
